title: Eviction hysteresis and admission smoothing to rescue mixed-deployment tail latency (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
A string of customer escalations this week (two Hosted customers, one Dedicated tenant on a mixed pool, and one Private on-prem deployment) converged on an intermittent tail-latency regression for long-context requests. Root cause analysis shows rapid cache-eviction bursts coupled with admission overshoot from the scheduler when Hosted burst capacity and Dedicated pinned capacity are both present on a node. The oscillation causes small short-lived requests to queue behind long-context inflight work, amplifying the long-context tail and creating KV cache churn that magnifies latency spikes.

Why this is urgent:
- Multiple customers reported production-facing P0 incidents impacting chat and summarization features.
- Observable impact across Hosted, Dedicated, and on-prem Private customers; Private sites with smaller KV budgets show worst effect.
- Automated autoscale and burst policies can mask the issue until traffic mixes heterogeneous lengths, making it a reproducible but intermittent fault.

Investigation highlights:
- Reproduced in staging by replaying mixed-length workload (40% short, 60% long) against a node with a pinned Dedicated pool alongside Hosted burst flows.
- Traces show repeated KV eviction waves each time admission allows an extra long-context batch; eviction delays subsequent batches by 60–450ms.
- Admission window currently computed from instantaneous free-GPU/slot tokens; no smoothing or hysteresis for eviction pressure.
- Private deployments observed more frequent thrash due to smaller KV cache and stricter memory limits.

Proposed fix(es):
1) Admission smoothing: introduce an EWMA over admission tokens with configurable alpha per deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private). Default alpha=0.3 for Hosted, 0.15 for Dedicated, 0.05 for Private to be conservative.
2) Eviction hysteresis: when an eviction event is detected, apply a short-term admission dampening (200–800ms, adaptive) to prevent immediate admission of additional long-context batches that would re-trigger thrash.
3) Per-tenant short-request fast-path: guarantee a small reservation for latency-sensitive short requests (configurable slot reserve, default 5% of capacity) and preemptively dequeue one short request when eviction pressure is high.
4) Monitoring & gates: add metrics (eviction_wave_count, eviction_pressure_score, admission_smoothing_active) and a canary guardrail to prevent rollout if 99th percentile latency increases beyond 10% for a 10-minute window.

Backward compatibility and deploy considerations:
- Changes are runtime guarded behind flags; default off for Private until validated.
- Hosted rollout will be canaryed in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 on low-traffic windows.
- Dedicated customers offered opt-in early access; Private customers will require agent/installer update notes and a per-site tuning guide.

Rollout plan:
- Stage (today): deploy smoothing + hysteresis behind flags to internal staging cluster; run mixed-length replay for 8 hours.
- Canary (72h): enable on 3 low-traffic Hosted clusters and one Dedicated small-pool tenant. Observe metrics and error budgets.
- Ramp (2 weeks): progressively enable with automatic rollback if guardrail triggers or customer reports regressions.

Testing strategy:
- Add CI replay harness test simulating mixed-length traffic with KV budget throttling to assert no eviction-wave cascading after fix.
- Add unit tests for EWMA computation and hysteresis timers.
- Run blackbox e2e against Private installer on a constrained VM.

Runbook (short):
- If 99th token latency rises > 25% post-rollout, flip runtime flag off for the cluster and collect a full trace.
- If eviction_pressure_score > 0.7 for > 60s, enable per-tenant short-request fast-path for the tenant and reduce admission alpha.

Related links:
- Staging replay script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-tests/compare/mixed-length-replay
- Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/eviction-oscillation
- Initial customer escalations (redacted): https://drive.redwood.ai/esc/esc-2026-03-09

Next steps (owners):
- ENG (Miguel Torres): implement EWMA admission and eviction hysteresis (PR target: runtime-2.5 branch).
- SRE (Lina Chow): configure staging canary and dashboards; run 8h replay.
- DX/SE (Ravi Menon): prepare customer-facing notes and Private site tuning doc.

Acceptance criteria:
- Staging replay shows reduction in eviction_wave_count by >= 80% and 99th token latency reduction >= 35% under mixed traffic.
- No more than one customer-reported recurrence in the 14-day post-rollout monitoring window.

Longer-term follow-ups (not blocking):
- Explore admission policies aware of KV footprint per request (cost-weighted admission).
- Consider kernel-level memory accounting hooks to more accurately predict eviction risk.
